chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Bazī‘, from al-Khaybarī, from Yūnus ibn Ḍabyān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, ‘May I be sacrificed for you, how is the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) performed in the state of Taqiyyah (precaution)?’ He said: ‘When you reach the Euphrates, perform Ghusl, then wear your purified garments [your two purified garments]. Then pass by opposite the grave and say: May Allāh’s blessings be upon you, O Abā ‘Abdillāh! May Allāh’s blessings be upon you, O Abā ‘Abdillāh! Then your Ziyārah is complete.’

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation or state of caution)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ: Ṣallā Allāhu ‘alayka (May Allah’s blessings be upon you)

ai.seo_question: How to perform Husayn's Ziyarah during Taqiyyah or times of fear?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the legal principle of *Ziyārah al-Qa’imah* (standing visitation) for Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) during periods of political danger or Taqiyyah, where the full ritual is impractical. It emphasizes that spiritual presence and sincere salutation, preceded by purification in the Euphrates, are sufficient to fulfill the religious obligation, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on accessibility of devotion amidst persecution.
